summary.headline: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee reviewed FY28 requests totaling $2.15 million in appropriations and up to $49 million in bondable projects.
summary.summary: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee met to conduct an initial review of department submissions for the FY28 capital plan. Departments submitted $2.152 million in potential cash appropriations and up to $49 million in bondable requests, which is heavily dominated by a $45 million placeholder for the Neary School building project. Committee members identified which department heads should be called in for live presentations, requesting vehicle inventories from Public Works and detailed quotes and photos from the school department. A joint presentation to the Select Board and Advisory Committee is planned for early December.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee opened the meeting and approved draft meeting minutes from January 12 and adopted the Select Board minutes from a previous joint meeting as requested by the town clerk.
key_details: Approved minutes of January 12th.
Adopted Select Board minutes from a past joint meeting.
A member experienced microphone connectivity issues during roll call, resolved shortly thereafter.

topics.title: FY28 capital plan overview and budget approach
topics.summary: The chair presented an overarching summary of all capital submissions compiled with automated tools from departmental spreadsheets. Submissions for FY28 currently stand at $2.152 million in potential appropriations and up to $49 million in bondable projects, dominated by school proposals. The committee discussed its strategy to vet and prioritize needs ahead of a joint presentation to the Select Board and Advisory Committee.
key_details: Total FY28 capital requests submitted for direct appropriation equal $2.152 million.
Total potential bondable project requests reach up to $49 million.
A placeholder of $45 million for the Neary School represents the vast majority of the bondable total.
Projects under $300,000 are currently categorized under direct appropriations.
A tentative placeholder presentation to the Select Board and Advisory Committee is set for December 1.
topics.outcome: Committee established review criteria and presentation expectations.
topics.why_it_matters: Capital requests directly determine town borrowing, tax levy burdens, and potential debt exclusion ballot questions for residents.

topics.title: School department capital requests
topics.summary: The committee reviewed capital items submitted for local Southborough public schools totaling $710,000. Members examined requests for stair and sink replacements and catch basin fencing, asking for photographic evidence, detailed quotes, and departmental prioritization.
key_details: Finn School bird bath sink replacement is requested at $120,000.
Finn School catch basin perimeter fencing is requested at $100,000.
Woodward School front stair replacement is requested at $250,000.
Trottier Middle School bird bath sink replacement is requested at $240,000.
Requests were submitted on time but have not yet been formally voted on by the School Committee.
topics.outcome: Committee requested written quotes, photos, and a representative from the school department to present.
topics.why_it_matters: School maintenance and renovations constitute a major portion of municipal capital spending.

topics.title: Recreation department capital requests
topics.summary: Members discussed recurring field and park maintenance allocations and checked the status of the proposed dog park project. The committee sought confirmation on whether the park maintenance line item is $25,000 or $50,000 in FY28.
key_details: Park maintenance fund was established two years ago and appears as either $25,000 or $50,000 depending on the spreadsheet tab.
Dog park funding remains before the Community Preservation Committee.
Members confirmed that if dog park funding is not supported by Community Preservation Act funds or grants, recreation will not seek town capital funds.
topics.outcome: The chair will verify the exact requested maintenance fund amount and confirm the dog park funding status.

topics.title: Fire department capital requests
topics.summary: The committee reviewed five capital items submitted by the Fire Department for FY28. Members agreed that written descriptions from the fire chief would be sufficient rather than requiring an in-person appearance.
key_details: Requests include a fire prevention vehicle at $27,000.
Other requests include an EM1 communications unit, a light tower, fire hose replacements, and an SCBA compressor fill station.
The chief is pursuing federal grant opportunities for fire hose and nozzle replacements.
topics.outcome: Committee will request written explanatory memos from the fire chief.

topics.title: Public Works capital requests
topics.summary: Public Works represents the largest department request, including fleet replacements and water system infrastructure. Members discussed the pace of heavy truck purchases and asked for an inventory and lifecycle plan to evaluate whether trucks should be replaced or refurbished.
key_details: General fund requests include two large dump/plow trucks at $275,000 each.
Additional general fund requests include a John Deere utility vehicle and a brine maker.
Water fund requests include road utility work on Parkerville Road and Waldi Court.
Bondable water items include water meter upgrades, the Fayville Tara Road tank, and Atwood tank cleanup.
topics.outcome: Committee requested DPW Director attend a meeting with a full vehicle inventory and replacement schedule.
topics.why_it_matters: Heavy DPW vehicles and water infrastructure investments involve hundreds of thousands of dollars in annual taxpayer and ratepayer costs.

topics.title: Facilities department capital requests
topics.summary: The committee evaluated requests submitted for municipal facilities maintenance and utility connections. The chair noted a formatting issue that will be cleaned up to distinguish recurring annual maintenance from bondable capital.
key_details: Cordaville Hall water service line replacement is requested at $30,000.
Facilities pickup truck replacement is requested at $70,000.
Facilities maintenance fund totals $125,000 and will be categorized under direct appropriations rather than debt.
topics.outcome: Committee requested written rationale for the truck and water service line replacements.

topics.title: Police department capital requests
topics.summary: The Police Department submitted requests for one cruiser and a multi-year lease program for tasers and body-worn cameras. The committee agreed to invite the police chief to explain ongoing lease obligations and camera storage requirements.
key_details: Police requested one patrol cruiser for FY28, down from past requests of two or three.
A holistic package replacement for tasers and body cameras is requested on a multi-year lease.
Initial body cameras were originally grant funded.
topics.outcome: Police chief will be invited to discuss the cruiser and taser and camera lease program.

topics.title: Regional school capital and Neary project outlook
topics.summary: Members discussed long-range school capital impacts, including the Regional School District assessment and the ongoing Neary School building study. The committee discussed scheduling a joint meeting with the Select Board and Advisory Committee before Thanksgiving to align on the town's financial capacity for major school projects.
key_details: Southborough covers approximately 40% of capital costs for the regional high school district based on enrollment formula.
The most expansive Neary project option currently carries a preliminary estimate of up to $45 million.
The Neary Building Committee recently received cost estimates including a $15 million option previously required by Town Meeting.
A joint committee meeting regarding Neary options is targeted before Thanksgiving.
topics.outcome: Committee will coordinate with the School Committee, Select Board, and Advisory Committee for a joint session.
topics.why_it_matters: A potential Neary building project would require a substantial debt exclusion and tax impact, affecting the town's capacity for other infrastructure investments.

Joint meeting with Select Board and Advisory Committee regarding Neary School project
Capital Committee presentation to the Select Board and Advisory Committee

summary.caveats: A committee member experienced a temporary audio malfunction during the opening roll call from 0:01:05 to 0:02:13, which was resolved before substantive capital discussions began.
